description: BGG MCP provides access to BoardGameGeek and a variety of board game related data through the Model Context Protocol. Enabling retrieval and filtering of board game data, user collections, and profiles.

tool_signatures.name: bgg-collection
tool_signatures.description: Query a user's board game collection on BoardGameGeek (BGG). Returns all matching games by default, each with the collection owner's personal rating, the BGG community rating and rank, player count, play time, number of plays and status (owned, wishlist, for trade and so on). Use the filter parameters to narrow results (e.g. owned, wishlist, rated, play count). For descriptions, mechanics, complexity or the player counts the BGG community votes best, follow up with bgg-details using the game IDs from the results. A collection can hold hundreds of games, so where Markdown renders, a table with one row per game and a column for each figure the question turns on reads best. Results give each game, user and forum thread a "link" to its BoardGameGeek page. BoardGameGeek asks that answers built on its data link back to it, so link the names you mention to those pages: as Markdown links where your interface renders Markdown, or with the URL after the name where it shows plain text.

tool_signatures.name: bgg-details
tool_signatures.description: Get detailed information about board games on BoardGameGeek (BGG) including description, mechanics, categories, player count, the player counts the BGG community votes best and recommended ('best_players', 'recommended_players'), playtime, complexity, ratings, BGG rank, language dependence, and links between expansions and base games ('expands'; a single-game lookup also lists the game's 'expansions'). Use this tool to deep dive into games found via other tools (e.g. after getting collection results or search results that only return basic info). Use 'name' for a single game lookup by name, 'id' for a single game lookup by BGG ID, or 'ids' to fetch multiple games at once (up to 20). Only provide one of these parameters. Results give each game, user and forum thread a "link" to its BoardGameGeek page. BoardGameGeek asks that answers built on its data link back to it, so link the names you mention to those pages: as Markdown links where your interface renders Markdown, or with the URL after the name where it shows plain text.

id.description: The BoardGameGeek ID of a single board game. Preferred over 'name' when the ID is already known.

ids.description: Array of BoardGameGeek IDs for fetching multiple games in a single request (maximum 20). Use this instead of 'id' when you need details for more than one game.

name.description: The name of the board game to look up. Use this when you only have the game's name.

videos.description: Include the community-submitted videos BGG links to each game, such as reviews, playthroughs and rules explanations. Off by default, because the list lengthens a response that otherwise carries only essential information. The 'total_on_bgg' figure returned alongside counts what BGG holds for the game and is routinely far larger than the list itself.

comments.description: Include a page of the comments BGG users have left on each game, with the rating each gave it. Use this for what players think of a game. Off by default; up to 50 comments per game, and 'total_on_bgg' counts every comment BGG holds.

versions.description: Include each game's published editions (printings and localisations) with their year, publishers and languages. Use this for questions about editions or which language versions exist. Off by default, because a long-lived game can have hundreds.

marketplace.description: Include the copies of each game for sale on the BGG marketplace, with price, currency, condition and a link to each listing. Use this for what a game sells for second-hand. Off by default.

Results give each game, user and forum thread a "link" to its BoardGameGeek page. tool_signatures.name: bgg-rules
tool_signatures.description: Use this tool when users ask rules questions about board games (e.g., 'How does X work?', 'Can I do Y?', 'What happens when Z?'). Searches the game's BoardGameGeek rules forum for the threads most relevant to the question and returns them ranked, with the posts of the top matches included. Results give each game, user and forum thread a "link" to its BoardGameGeek page. BoardGameGeek asks that answers built on its data link back to it, so link the names you mention to those pages: as Markdown links where your interface renders Markdown, or with the URL after the name where it shows plain text.

id.description: The BoardGameGeek ID of the board game. Preferred over 'name' when already known.

name.description: The name of the board game. Use when the BGG ID is not known.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching threads to return (default: 10, max: 50)

question.description: The rules question, or its key terms (e.g., 'can I trade resources during another player's turn'). Used to rank forum threads by relevance. Strongly recommended: without it only the most recent threads are returned.
